title: Traction Microscopy Integrated with Microfluidics for Chemotactic Collective Migration
protocol: Design the micropattern of stencil and microchannel.
Fabricate or outsource SU-8 molds (thickness of ~250 μm for stencils and ~150 μm for microchannels) on silicon wafers (4" diameter).
Prepare PDMS mixture by mixing the base elastomer and curing agent at a ratio of 10:1.
Vortex the PDMS mixture for 5 min.
Centrifuge the PDMS mixture at 196 x g for 1 min to remove bubbles.
Pour ~1 mL of the PDMS mixture on the wafer, while avoiding SU-8 patterned regions so that the PDMS touches the side of the SU-8 pillars but not the top of the SU-8 pattern.
Place the wafer on a flat surface for over 30 min at room temperature (RT).
Cure the PDMS in a dry oven at 80 °C for over 2 h.
Carefully peel off the PDMS from SU-8 mold and trim the thin PDMS membrane using a 14 mm hollow punch.
Remove the dust on the surface of the PDMS pieces using sticky tape and autoclave the PDMS stencils.
Pour ~30 mL of PDMS mixture over the SU-8 mold.
Degas for 30 min in a vacuum chamber.
Cure the PDMS in a dry oven at 80 °C for over 2 hours.
Carefully peel off the PDMS from SU-8 mold.
Cut the PDMS to a size of 24 mm x 24 mm.
Create one outlet and three inlets using a 1 mm biopsy punch in each PDMS block.
Manufacture or outsource rectangular slide glasses (24 mm x 24 mm x 1 mm) with a rectangular micro-well (6 mm x 12 mm, 100 μm depth).
Silanize the surface of a bottom glass.
Prepare a bind silane solution by mixing 200 mL of deionized water (DIW), 80 μL of acetic acid, and 50 µL of 3-(trimethoxysilyl) propyl methacrylate (TMSPMA).
Remove the dust from the surface of the glass by sticky tape.
Autoclave the glass.
Cover the etched surface of the bottom glass with 100 μL of the bind silane solution.
Leave the glass at RT for 1 hour.
Rinse the glass with DIW three times.
Let the glass dry at ambient air temperature or by blowing air.
Prepare a fresh solution of 0.5 % (w/v) ammonium persulfate (APS) by dissolving 5 mg of APS in 1 mL of DIW.
Prepare the PA gel solution consisting of 138 µL of 40% acrylamide solution, 101 µL of 2% bis-acrylamide solution, 5 µL of fluorescent particle solution (0.2 μm), and 655 µL of DIW.
Wear protective gloves, clothing, and eye protection when handling acrylamide and bisacrylamide solutions.
Vortex the fluorescent bead solution before pipetting to obtain a uniform number of fluorescent beads per batch.
Add 100 μL of APS solution to the PA gel solution.
Add 1 μL of tetramethylethylenediamine (TEMED) to the mixed gel solution.
Transfer 10 µL of mixed gel solution onto the rectangular micro-well.
Place a circular coverslip on top of the micro-well containing the gel solution.
Place sufficient gel solution on the groove of the bottom glass, carefully slide the coverslip over the gel solution and remove excess gel solution to avoid bubbles.
Centrifuge the assembly for 10 min at 96 x g to bring fluorescent particles to the top layer of PA gel.
Flip the assembly after centrifuging and place it in a 35 mm Petri dish.
Fill the Petri dish with 2 mL of DIW.
Gently remove the coverslip by sliding it to one side using forceps.
Dissolve 1 mg/mL sulfosuccinimidyl 6-(4'-azido-2'-nitrophenylamino) hexanoate (sulfo-SANPAH) in warm 50 mM HEPES buffer.
Drop 200 μL of the sulfo-SANPAH solution onto the gel surface and activate by UV light for 10 min at 365 nm wavelength.
Rinse the gel with 0.1 M HEPES buffer twice and with PBS once.
Coat the PA gel with collagen solution (100 μg/mL in PBS, rat tail collagen type I) at 4 °C overnight.
Wash the PA gel with PBS three times on the following day.
Prepare F-127 solution [2% (w/v) in PBS].
Immerse the autoclaved PDMS stencil in the F-127 solution and incubate it in a 37 °C incubator for 1 h.
Prepare cell solution (2 x 10^6 cells/mL) in DMEM with 10% fetal bovine serum and 1% antibiotic-antimycotic.
Wash the PDMS stencil with PBS three times and remove liquid from both the PDMS stencil and PA gel.
Place the PDMS stencil on the PA gel and add PBS to the stencil.
Remove bubbles in the holes of PDMS stencil by pipetting gently.
Remove PBS from the surface of the PDMS stencil.
Put 200 µL of cell solution on PDMS stencil.
Incubate PA gel with attached cells in an incubator for 1 hour.
Gently wash off cell solution with cell culture media.
Remove the PDMS stencil from the PA gel.
Add more cell culture media to the PA gel.
Check the formation of cell islands under a microscope.
Remove dust on the PDMS microchannel using sticky tape.
Autoclave the PDMS microchannel.
Treat the surface of the PDMS microchannel with oxygen plasma (80 W, 50 kHz) for 30 seconds.
Remove any fluid from the PA gel-filled bottom glass.
Place the PDMS microchannel on top of the bottom glass.
Put the assembly on a custom glass holder.
Fill the microchannel with cell culture medium.
Flush warm media through the channels to remove bubbles gently.
Trim the tip of needles (18 G) and bend them 90° for connectors.
Prepare tubing lines for three inlets using trimmed needle, mini-volume line, and three-way stopcock.
Prepare one outlet tubing line using trimmed needle, mini-volume line, and three-way stopcock.
Fill the tubing lines with preheated medium that has been warmed for 1 hour.
Remove all bubbles trapped in the tubing lines by gently flushing warm media with a syringe.
Prepare reservoirs by removing plungers from syringes and connecting inlet tubing lines.
Plug the needle connectors of each tubing line into the three inlets and one outlet of the microfluidic device.
Fill the reservoirs with 3 mL of fresh medium or conditioned medium each.
For the gradient test, fill the left inlet reservoir with 20 ng/mL HGF in the cell culture medium.
For the visualization of concentration gradient, add a 200 µg/mL fluorescent dye (rhodamine B-dextran, 70 kDa) to the left inlet reservoir.
Connect the outlet tubing line to a syringe pump.
Place the integrated microfluidic system on the stage of a conventional epifluorescent microscope.
Set the operating mode of the syringe pump to "withdrawal".
Generate a gentle gradient of HGF in the microfluidic channel at a flow rate of 0.1 µL/min.
Stabilize the gradient for 2 hours before starting the experiment.
Avoid physical disturbance during the stabilization period and throughout the experiment.
Take images every 10 minutes for up to 24 hours using an automated microscope housed in an incubator.
Use a 4x objective lens to capture three different channels at each timepoint.
Capture phase image to visualize cell migration.
Capture green fluorescent image to visualize fluorescent beads embedded in PA gel.
Capture red fluorescent image to visualize the concentration gradient of a chemical.
Infuse 0.25% trypsin-EDTA solution into microchannels to detach cells from the PA gel.
Completely remove cells from the gel.
Take a green fluorescent image as a reference for traction microscopy.
